question: The SI unit of 'ultimate stress' is ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __pascal (Pa).__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Ultimate stress__ is the maximum stress that a material can withstand before failing.
 
• The unit of ultimate stress is pascal (Pa), which is equivalent to N/m² (newton per square meter).
 
• It is a measure of the strength of a material under tension or compression.
 
• It is an important parameter in material science and engineering applications.
 
• Ultimate stress values vary depending on the material and its properties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Stress:**

 
 
• Stress is defined as force per unit area and is expressed in pascal (Pa).
 
• It can be classified into tensile stress, compressive stress, and shear stress.
 
 
 
• **Strain:**
 
 
• It is the deformation or change in shape and size of a material due to applied stress.
 
• Strain is a dimensionless quantity and is often expressed as a ratio.
 
 
 
• **Elasticity:**
 
 
• Elasticity is the property of a material to return to its original shape and size after the removal of stress.
 
• Materials with high elasticity are used in applications requiring flexibility and durability.
